passages.title: From school to university: a path with choices
passages.text:
[A] A student who wants to continue studying after secondary school can choose from several routes. Some apply directly to university, while others take a practical course or work for a year first. The best decision depends on the student's interests, family circumstances and the qualifications required for a particular occupation. A young person interested in nursing, for example, may need a recognised professional degree, whereas someone interested in graphic design may first build a portfolio through a shorter programme. Neither route guarantees a job, and it is unhelpful to describe one as suitable for everyone.
[B] Before submitting an application, students should investigate entry requirements. These may include previous examination results, evidence of language ability and a personal statement. A university may also request a portfolio or invite applicants to an interview. In a fictional survey at Brookford College, advisers found that students who began researching options early were more likely to submit complete applications. However, the survey did not establish that early preparation caused higher admission rates. Students with greater support at home may simply have found the process easier.
[C] Costs deserve the same attention as entry requirements. Tuition fees are only one part of the budget. Students who leave home must allow for accommodation, food, transport and study materials. At many institutions, financial support is available, but eligibility rules vary. Some awards are based on academic achievement, while others consider household income. Students should confirm the conditions of any grant rather than assume that financial support will cover every expense. An adviser can explain the available options, although the student remains responsible for checking official deadlines.
[D] After receiving an offer, an applicant may need to accept the place and supply evidence of earlier qualifications. International students can face extra administrative stages, including immigration permission. It is important not to book an expensive journey before checking the relevant requirements. Once enrolled, new students usually receive information about induction events and learning support. These activities introduce services such as the library, academic writing centre and wellbeing team. They are useful even for students who already know the city.
[E] The transition to university also changes the way learning happens. At school, a teacher may check homework every day. At university, lecturers introduce ideas in larger sessions, but students are expected to organise much of their reading independently. Tutorials provide a smaller setting in which students question evidence, test explanations and receive feedback. An assignment should show the student's reasoning, not merely repeat a lecturer's words. Effective students often plan their week around deadlines rather than waiting until an examination approaches.
[F] Finally, no route should be judged only by the name of its qualification. Employers may value practical experience, communication and reliable work habits alongside academic results. A graduate who has completed a placement can sometimes explain a workplace problem more clearly than someone who has studied only from books. Equally, theoretical knowledge may be essential in professions where mistakes could cause harm. The sensible approach is to compare course content, support, cost and future opportunities, then make a decision that can be reviewed as circumstances change.

coach.message: Bài “Flow-chart and course applications”: Sau bài học, học viên có thể: Lập trình tự entry requirements → application → conditional portfolio/interview tùy ngành. Đồng thời tự phát hiện lỗi: Không… Trước khi thử, hãy nói một việc bạn sẽ kiểm tra ở bài này.

Bạn đang xem “entrance examination” (noun phrase), nghĩa là “kỳ thi tuyển sinh”. Ví dụ: “Some programmes require an entrance examination.”. Hãy tạo một câu mới liên quan đến flow-chart and course applications thay vì chép lại.

Ở ví dụ có hướng dẫn “What comes after checking requirements for some applicants?”, hãy làm bước này trước: Đọc câu hỏi trước để xác định cần tìm quan điểm, địa điểm, số liệu hay ý chính. Chỉ mở mẫu sau khi tự thử.

Lỗi dễ gặp ở bài “Flow-chart and course applications”: Không biến bước có điều kiện thành bắt buộc cho mọi ứng viên. Lỗi xuất hiện khi áp dụng chiến lược Application routes and flow chart mà không xét đầy đủ ngữ cảnh.

Bạn đã hoàn thành bài “Flow-chart and course applications”. Hãy đánh dấu bằng chứng trong văn bản; lưu cụm “entrance examination” nếu thực sự muốn dùng lại, rồi sửa một chỗ chưa chắc chắn trước khi làm bài mới.
Bài này mình luyện Flow-chart Completion – Admission Routes. Hãy đọc đoạn rồi tìm phần nào trả lời đúng câu hỏi; chưa cần đoán ngay.
Bạn đang bị bẫy: portfolio: chỉ dùng cho một số course. Hãy đọc bằng chứng “first check the entry requirements online” rồi thử lại.
Hãy phân biệt: Yes: bỏ qua điều kiện design courses. Bằng chứng cần đối chiếu là “Applicants for other programmes receive a decision without these extra steps”.
Bạn đã tìm đúng cả hai bằng chứng. Hãy vào phần luyện độc lập; Coach sẽ không tự chen vào.

Hôm nay mình học Application routes and flow chart. Hãy thử tìm trong tình huống này điều quan trọng nhất: “Applicants first check entry requirements. Some are then asked for a portfolio before an interview is scheduled.”
Bạn đang gặp bẫy của bài này: Không biến bước có điều kiện thành bắt buộc cho mọi ứng viên. Mình gợi ý: Trace the order markers first/then/before, and keep the conditional “some”.
Đừng mở đáp án vội. Với câu “What comes after checking requirements for some applicants?”, hãy thử chọn một cụm trong nguồn rồi giải thích vì sao nó phù hợp.
Bài này hãy nhớ: Trace the order markers first/then/before, and keep the conditional “some”. Bạn có thể lưu cụm “admissions” rồi nói hoặc viết lại một câu của riêng mình.
